beginner.summary: For developers, QA engineers, data analysts and product people who build or test applications on large language models and have never measured one rigorously. Covers why LLM output cannot be tested like ordinary code, the anatomy of an eval, hand-built golden datasets, programmatic and overlap metrics, confidence intervals for pass rates, first LLM-as-judge rubrics and pairwise comparison, public benchmarks with lm-evaluation-harness, promptfoo, DeepEval, Inspect and OpenAI Evals, error analysis, and a capstone that evaluates a ticket summariser.
prerequisites: Writes and runs small Python 3.12 scripts, installs packages with pip and reads JSON and CSV files
Has called a hosted LLM API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible local server such as Ollama) at least once, or can follow a short guide to do so
Knows basic percentages and averages; no statistics background is assumed
outcomes: Explain why LLM outputs need datasets, scorers and statistics, and describe a run as dataset, task, scorer and aggregate
Build a versioned golden dataset and score it with exact-match, schema, overlap and embedding metrics, reporting every pass rate with a confidence interval
Run a first rubric-based LLM judge and a pairwise comparison and recognise position bias
Operate promptfoo, DeepEval, Inspect and lm-evaluation-harness on a small task and write a failure taxonomy from error analysis
